locator: V.5, 1015a20-b15 (the senses of the necessary), with IX.8, 1050b6-18 and XII.7, 1072b10-13
goal: Look for a source of the open bridge STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE (whatever can fail to be r can be otherwise in respect r), which carries the Lambda.7 route to the first mover's pure act (ARIST-MET-XII-7-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT). Delta.5, 1015a33-36 defines the necessary as what cannot be otherwise (τὸ μὴ ἐνδεχόμενον ἄλλως ἔχειν); Theta.8 says what can be can both be and not be. A reading that ties the two per respect (what can not be r can be otherwise in r) would source the bridge; a reading that ties them only for being simply (substance) would not. Pin V.5 in the Perseus witness, read it with IX.8 and XII.7, and record whichever holds. Do not identify CanFailToBe with CanBeOtherwise by definition (DISAMB-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-OR-BE-OTHERWISE).
reason: The Lambda.7 route replaces act's simple priority, non-simultaneity and the first-being bridge with two sourced readings, the already-paid uniqueness premise and this one bare bridge. In Metaph. XII, lect. 7 n. 13-15 was checked and does not supply it (its two glosses of the necessary are applied to different things).
